anomaly_def.Name: Optimizer Statistics Anomaly + Buffer Cache and Latch Contention Anomaly + Data Block and Index Integrity Anomaly
anomaly_def.Description:
Optimizer Statistics Anomaly : Stale or incomplete statistics cause systematic cardinality misestimation, leading the optimizer to choose sub-optimal access paths and join orders.
Buffer Cache and Latch Contention Anomaly : Hot pages, undersized cache, or slow I/O make sessions frequently block or spin on page pins, latches, or buffer I/O slots.
Data Block and Index Integrity Anomaly : Physical corruption or logical structural inconsistency in data pages or index pages breaks the trustworthiness of persisted storage structures.

When all three anomalies coexist, the system exhibits a mixture of plan instability, erratic execution latency, and intermittent correctness failures. Queries may pick inefficient plans because of bad statistics, then spend excessive time waiting on buffer-busy or page-latch events once those plans hammer a small set of corrupted or hot pages. Corrupted index structures can amplify misestimation by returning duplicate or missing rows, causing row-count feedback to diverge even further from reality. Meanwhile, latch contention is magnified by repeated retries, table scans, or forced full-index rebuilds triggered by corruption detection; CPU usage spikes, I/O throughput plateaus, and error logs intermittently show checksum or key-order violations alongside bursts of statistics-related recompiles.

Causally, stale statistics direct traffic toward the wrong objects or access patterns, concentrating activity on a subset of pages and thereby creating hotspots that intensify latch contention. Prolonged contention increases buffer churn and I/O latency, stretching checkpoint and recovery windows and making corruption-prone pages stay dirty longer, raising the risk of incomplete writes or torn pages that deepen structural damage. Conversely, hidden corruption can distort sampling when statistics are collected, producing even worse estimates and feeding a feedback loop of poor plan choices. Together, these interactions degrade both performance and data correctness far more severely than any single anomaly would, complicating diagnosis because symptoms from one layer disguise or trigger failures in the others.

entry.official_description: Foreign key constraint for table '%.192s', record '%-.192s' would lead to a duplicate entry in table '%.192s', key '%.192s'
entry.cause_analysis: The failure is typically associated with logical data inconsistency, structural corruption, uniqueness conflicts, or referential-integrity rules being violated by the workload or storage state.
entry.solution_guidance: Validate data consistency, inspect constraints and index integrity, and check whether data-cleaning, repair, or workload correction is required before retrying.
